commits.messageBody:
Adopted as a DESIGN NOTE. Not promoted to a fourth clause of constitution
invariant 2; promote and decline were both rejected. Founder decision
2026-09-23, taken on the three costed options already stated in the record.

So the wording is guidance, not an invariant: it gates nothing, no check
enforces it, and contradicting it is not a constitution violation. What it
buys is that the shape stops being re-derived.

Evidence added after the proposal was written, which is why the note is
recorded rather than dropped: on 2026-09-22 the drain hit its own 8-hour
lifetime backstop and stopped. It satisfied ALL THREE existing DR-066
clauses - failed closed, logged the stop visibly, witness had two producers -
and then sat idle with 90 issues queued until a human happened to start a
session. Nothing broken, nothing violated. That is the gap.

The stated cost is real and is now the open problem, filed as #2081: an
unenforced prose rule drifts, and clause 1 already proved it here - prose for
two months, six hand-fixes, then a lint found fifteen more unremarked
violations. Expect the same, and the note says so in its own body rather than
leaving a reader to assume it carries weight it does not.

`status:` deliberately untouched. The founder settled the liveness clause,
which is not the same act as accepting DR-093; that remains a separate human
step via MinSpec: Accept ADR, per DR-029, and no agent may mint it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: docs(#1859): record the founder's decision on DR-093's liveness clause

commits.messageBody:
…nd pending

Both reviewers blocked on the same contradiction, and they were right: the new
Decision section records the liveness clause as settled, while the untouched
Follow-ups bullet still read "needs a human decision... deliberately not
self-applied here." The record asserted both at once, in a document whose only
job is to be accurate.

Four stale spots, not the one that was cited:

- The Follow-ups bullet now records the outcome (design note adopted; promote
  and decline rejected) instead of the open question.
- The section preamble said "This section is the *proposal*". Past tense now,
  with a pointer to the Decision block.
- "Recommendation: adopt it" now reads as the recommendation that was put to the
  founder, and says it was the option taken.
- The #1855/#1853 bullet said the section "proposes amending" DR-066. It no
  longer does, and the amendment was the rejected option, so that cross-reference
  was newly false as well.

Also adds #2081 as its own Follow-ups bullet. It was cited only inline in the
Decision section, which DR-023 does not accept: a follow-up that lives in prose
is the leak that rule exists to close.

On the architect's non-blocking provenance point: added a paragraph saying
plainly that the diff cannot evidence a decision taken in session, so a reviewer
sees only an agent asserting a human choice. It invites confirmation at merge and
states the narrow reading, that this settles the liveness question and does not
accept DR-093.

status: proposed is still untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: docs(#1859): stop DR-093 saying the liveness decision is both taken a…

commits.messageBody:
The decision section this PR adds says twice that DR-093 "stays
`proposed`". That was true when it was written on 2026-09-24, but #2076
accepted DR-093 on main (d1b5ceb3, 2026-09-27), so once merged the record
would contradict its own `status: accepted` and its Status section.

Reword only those two claims. The point they make is kept: settling the
liveness clause is not the act that accepted DR-093. That was a separate
human act via MinSpec: Accept ADR, taken in #2076.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
